🐛 Describe the bug
I into this weird JIT bug a while back and reduced it into a minimal example today. Consider the expression a + (b / (-b))[:] where a and b are tensors of appropriate shape. If we put this expression into a function and JIT compile it, it will work with the following caveat: If the JIT compilation is triggered by a call where a.requires_grad, the compiled function will always return a tensor that .requires_grad and has a backward graph attached, regardless of any of the inputs requiring gradients or not. Triggering the JIT compilation with tensors that do not require gradients will produce a function that behaves as expected. Curiously, the behavior depends upon the formulation of the operations on b, the tensor that does not even require a gradient. If we remove the minus, for example, a + (b / b)[:] or move the minus into a different position a + (-(b / b)[:]), JIT compilation works as expected.
The code below reproduces this behavior. It says that a function "fails", if JIT compiling it with grad-requiring tensors makes it always return grad-requiring tensors, and it "works" otherwise.
import torch

def check_no_grad(f):
    f_ = torch.jit.script(f)

    y = torch.ones(1)
    t = torch.ones(1)
    assert not t.requires_grad

    y.requires_grad_()
    assert y.requires_grad
    assert f_(y, t).requires_grad

    y.requires_grad_(False)
    assert not y.requires_grad
    if f_(y, t).requires_grad:
        print(f.__name__, "fails")
    else:
        print(f.__name__, "works")

def works_1(a, b):
    x = b / (-b)
    return a + x

def works_2(a, b):
    x = (b / b)[:]
    return a + x

def works_3(a, b):
    x = -(b / b)[:]
    return a + x

def fail_1(a, b):
    x = (b / (-b))[:]
    return a + x

check_no_grad(works_1)
check_no_grad(works_2)
check_no_grad(works_3)
check_no_grad(fail_1)

works_1 works
works_2 works
works_3 works
fail_1 fails

PyTorch should have publicly visible process of development that is consistent with reality. As of Aug 10, 2022 according to the public site (that is current source of truth) we have only following three types of the folks who participate in the development of the PyTorch:

Core contributors (out of scope of this bug)
Contributors - have super powers to approve PRs to be merged in
Developers - anyone else (no any permissions available except generic things like: open PR, create issues, etc)

However this source of truth is inconsistent with the reality, as of today we have following places that includes different people per different modules:

bug with mapping between labels modules and owners - used to ping people for new PR with a specific label
CODEOWNERS file - used for ppl to get notifications for files changes.
Persons of interest  site that has people that should have permissions to review in merge in changes
List of people who can actually merge changes

These places are inconsistent. There is also no clarity when/how each of them should be changed (or who should be changing them). The only clear thing is so far (according to the official site):

Persons of interest  is the page that has people that should have permissions to review in merge in changes. This site is updates after quarterly meetings of core maintainers and should be used as a source of truth.

Proposal
Proposing the following:

align all places on the modules names, there is no reason to have completely different modules (and even with different names for the same modules)
Governance site should point to merge_rules instead of CODEOWNERS file as a list of contributors, since merge_rules is the place that actually defines permissions to merge in
CODEOWNERS file should have a clear comment at the top indicating that this file used ONLY for the sake of people subscribing on the notification for the specific changes of specific files

🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Since DDP and FSDP are class wrappers, some nn.Module APIs may additional prefixing or otherwise not work in an equivalent fashion to local nn.Module instances due to the wrapping nature. This can cause some pain points in composing the modules together, checkpointing with state_dict, or any code that relies on module / parameter names / APIs such as named_parameters. This issue is to track what we can do for DDP / FSDP for each API. I've attempted to document current status below:
-- DDP --

state_dict / load_state_dict: Adds module prefix, but this can be worked around and stripped out with a flag or env variable (needs a PR to enable).
named_parameters / named_buffers - Adds module prefix as well
named_modules / modules() - includes DDP wrapped module as well, wrapped module is prefixed with "module"
children() - returns wrapped module and its children, whereas we might just want to return the wrapped module's children if we want equivalence to local

-- FSDP --

state_dict / load_state_dict: There are various ways to checkpoint, but full_state_dict and sharded_state_dict should checkpoint with original parameter names
named_parameters / named_buffers - In summon_full_params context, equivalent to local module checkpoint. Otherwise, flat_param type info is returned. @awgu is working on exposing original parameters which may help alleviate this issue
named_modules / modules() - same as DDP, includes wrapped module as well, and all nested FSDP wrappers.
children() - returns wrapped module and its children, same as DDP.

Also, we should check what these APIs do when DDP / FSDP is not the top-level module and just a non-root in the module hierarchy. It is not guaranteed that these APIs would remain the same.

📚 The doc issue
The documentation for F.batch_norm claims that it uses the biased estimator:

The standard-deviation is calculated via the biased estimator, equivalent to torch.var(input, unbiased=False)

However, a simple test shows that it actually uses the unbiased estimator:
x = torch.rand((100, 3, 10, 10))
unbiased_var = x.var((0, 2, 3), unbiased=True)
biased_var = x.var((0, 2, 3), unbiased=False)
mean = torch.zeros(3)
var = torch.ones(3)
F.batch_norm(x, 
    running_mean=mean, running_var=var, 
    training=True, momentum=1.0)
uses_unbiased_var = torch.allclose(var, unbiased_var)
uses_biased_var = torch.allclose(var, biased_var)
assert uses_biased_var, "Uh oh, batch_norm should use biased var"
Suggest a potential alternative/fix
Update the documentation for BatchNorm1D, BatchNorm2D, and BatchNorm3D to say that batch_norm uses the unbiased variance estimator:

The standard-deviation is calculated via the unbiased estimator, equivalent to torch.var(input, unbiased=True)

🐛 Describe the bug
When compiling LibTorch as a static lib (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF) on Windows 11, there is an issue with the static initialization.  Here is a small example how to reproduce this issue:
Create Conda env
conda create -n pytorch_build python=3.10
conda activate pytorch_build
conda install pyyaml typing_extensions

Build LibTorch and e.g. op_registration_test
For simplicity, we are building LibTorch (CPU only, without MKL etc.) and a single test target from the Caffe2_CPU_TEST_SRCS. I am using plain CMake, Ninja and MSVC compiler.
# clone repo
git clone --recursive https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch

# configure and build
cmake -G Ninja -S pytorch -B pytorch-build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=pytorch-install -DUSE_CUDA=OFF -DUSE_DISTRIBUTED=OFF -DUSE_TENSORPIPE=OFF -USE_MAGMA=OFF -DUSE_NUMPY=OFF -DUSE_OPENMP=OFF -DUSE_KINETO=OFF -DUSE_QNNPACK=OFF -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DBUILD_PYTHON=OFF -DBUILD_CAFFE2_OPS=OFF -DBUILD_TEST=ON -DUSE_FBGEMM=OFF -Wno-dev -DMSVC_Z7_OVERRIDE=OFF -DCAFFE2_USE_MSVC_STATIC_RUNTIME=OFF -Dprotobuf_MSVC_STATIC_RUNTIME=OFF
cmake --build pytorch-build --target op_registration_test

When running pytorch-build/bin/op_registration_test.exe in the console, you will see no output. When having a closer look by opening the executable in Visual Studio and running it under the debugger, we get the error message
"Type class c10::intrusive_ptr<struct LinearPackedParamsBase,struct c10::detail::intrusive_target_default_null_type<struct LinearPackedParamsBase> > could not be converted to any of the known types."

For more detail, see the full call stack here.
The problem seems to be that some of the statically initialized classes (LinearPackedParamsBase and ConvPackedParamsBase to be specific) are not initialized before some of their usage in a TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL definition. These problematic sections are:

aten/src/ATen/native/quantized/qlinear_unpack.cpp
aten/src/ATen/native/quantized/qconv_unpack.cpp
aten/src/ATen/native/quantized/cpu/qlinear_prepack.cpp
aten/src/ATen/native/quantized/cpu/qlinear_dynamic.cpp
aten/src/ATen/native/quantized/cpu/qlinear.cpp
aten/src/ATen/native/ao_sparse/quantized/cpu/qlinear_unpack.cpp
aten/src/ATen/native/ao_sparse/quantized/cpu/qlinear_prepack.cpp
aten/src/ATen/native/ao_sparse/quantized/cpu/qlinear.cpp

Specifically calling the construct on first use initialization functions (register_linear_params() and register_conv_params<>()) from the corresponding namespace at the top of the TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL body in above files fixes the issue. I have a PR ready that can fix this but I am wondering if there might be a better solution to this problem 😃

🐛 Describe the bug
@onnxbot
On the onnx site they asked me to post this here.
In the specific case of a PyTorch model with a Conv2d and a BatchNorm2d if onnx export is run on an M1 GPU mps model then a subsequent forward using onnx will not match a forward in PyTorch. If the same model is on the CPU or on CUDA then the export will produce a model that matches PyTorch. Note that PyTorch forwards on MPS and on CPU match in this case.
The example below shows my best effort at a minimum case. There needs to be more than one feature on the BatchNorm2d. You have to perform one forward before using eval() on the model so that the BatchNorm does a computation.
import copy
import torch
import torch
from torch import nn
import numpy as np
import os, sys
import onnx
import onnxruntime

y = torch.randn(1, 2, 3, 6)
device = 'cuda'
ygpu = y.to(device=device)
#conv = nn.Conv2d(in_channels=57, out_channels=1, kernel_size=(1,3), stride=2)
gpuconv = nn.Sequential(
nn.Conv2d(2, 2, stride=1, kernel_size=3),
nn.BatchNorm2d(num_features=2)
).to(device=device)
xgpu = gpuconv(ygpu)
gpuconv.eval()
xgpu = gpuconv(ygpu)
conv = copy.deepcopy(gpuconv).to(device='cpu')
x = conv(y)

print(torch.allclose(x, xgpu.to(device='cpu'), rtol=1e-03, atol=1e-05))
torch.onnx.export(conv, y, 'test.onnx', export_params=True)
torch.onnx.export(gpuconv, ygpu, 'testgpu.onnx', export_params=True)
onnx_model = onnx.load('testgpu.onnx')
onnx.checker.check_model(onnx_model)

ort_session = onnxruntime.InferenceSession('testgpu.onnx')

def to_numpy(tensor):

WLOG suppose we have a world size of 2.

The original parameter (i.e. the linear's weight) is like [[X]] where X is some initial value and the shape is [1, 1].
The unpadded unsharded flattened parameter is like [X] where the shape is [1].
The padded unsharded flattened parameter is like [X, 0] where the shape is [2]. (For larger world sizes, we pad more like [X, 0, 0, 0] for world size of 4.)
After we run on both ranks
with torch.no_grad():
    p[0] = self.rank + 2

rank 0's local shard is [2], and rank 1's local shard is [3].
When we run on both ranks

    with torch.no_grad():
       p.copy_(torch.zeros_like(p))

(code0, code1) In other words, if you print p in the summon_full_params() context, you see [2] for both rank 0 and rank 1. This means that the copy_() writes to the 0th element for both ranks. There is not an attempt to zero the 1st element of the padded unsharded flattened parameter.

Personally, I am not sure if FSDP should make any guarantees on persisting writes to the padding. It does not seem like a real use case.

🐛 Describe the bug
In the last step of fx graph mode quantization, we need to fuse a "reference quantized pattern" to a real quantized op. More details about reference quantized pattern can be found in https://github.com/pytorch/rfcs/blob/master/RFC-0019-Extending-PyTorch-Quantization-to-Custom-Backends.md
# Example flow of current code:
input - (fp32) linear1 -- (fp32) -- output1
  \ -- (fp32) linear2 -- (fp32) -- output2

# After prepare (observed model):
input - observer1 - linear1 --observer2 --output1
                  \ --- linear2 -- observer3 -- output2

# After convert_to_reference:
input - (fp32) - quantize1 --(int8) -- dequantize1 - linear1 --quantize2 -- (int8) -- dequantize2 - (fp32) - output1
                                       \ --(int8) -- linear2 -- quantize3 - dequantize3 - (fp32) -  output2

# After lowering:
# recognize the pattern "dequantize - linear - quantize" and fuse it to "quantized_linear"
# because dequantize is used by multiple linear in this example, to get the pattern we will replicate the dequantize node:
input - quantize1 - dequantize1 - linear1 --quantize2 - dequantize2 - output1
                        \ - dequantize1_1  --- linear2 -- quantize3 - dequantize3 - output2

# now we can fuse:
input - quantize1 - (int8) - quantize_linear1 (int8) - dequantize2 - output1
                        \ - (int8) - quantize_linear2 (int8) - dequantize3 - output2

e.g. the following pattern:
input - dequantize - fp32_operator - quantize - output

will be fused into
input - quantized_operator - output

However, since the dequantize op can be used by multiple ops, we can't simply fuse it:
input - dequantize - fp32_operator - quantize - output
               \ -- "some other op"

because "some other op" needs the output of dequantize as well. That's why we run the duplicate_dequantize_node pass to make sure each dequantize is only used by one node:
input - dequantize - fp32_operator - quantize - output
       \ - dequantize -- "some other op"

so that we can fuse the first dequantize.
However duplicating nodes means we also need to remove the node in the end if dequantize is not a part of a patter, that's why we need "remove_extra_dequantize" pass in the end. This is not scalable since for each type of node we will need to do the same trick.
A easier solution is to change the fusion logic, (since we are implementing fusion logic manually anyways), what we can do is:
given the following pattern:
input - dequantize - fp32_operator - quantize - output
                          \ -- "some other op"

we fuse the "dq - fp32_op - q" pattern, but we still keep the dequantize op, the result will look like the following:
     quantized_operator - output
     /
input - dequantize
                          \ -- "some other op"

Basically the fused quantized_operator is not connected to input after fusion.
Steps:


familiarize with torch.fx
https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch-fx


get familiar with this lowering code
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/_lower_to_native_backend.py#L514


remove duplicate_quantize_dynamic_node and repeat the process
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/_lower_to_native_backend.py#L566-L570
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/_lower_to_native_backend.py#L765-L772


compile again, run the fx tests:


python test/test_quantization.py TestQuantizeFx
python test/test_quantization.py TestQuantizeFxOps
python test/test_quantization.py TestQuantizeFxModels

when there are errors, fix the lowering code in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/_lower_to_native_backend.py and make sure the test still passes

in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/_lower_to_native_backend.py#L653-L660, instead of removing dequantize, we'll replace the input of quantized op (func_node) with the input of dequantize (dqn_input), by calling: https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/fx.html#torch.fx.Node.replace_input_with


remove duplicate_quantize_dynamic_node and repeat the process
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/_lower_to_native_backend.py#L566-L570
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/_lower_to_native_backend.py#L765-L772


remove the call to duplicate_dequantize_node and remove_extra_dequantize
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/convert.py#L797-L801


Versions
master
cc @jerryzh168 @jianyuh @raghuramank100 @jamesr66a @vkuzo
